A mandalart is a frame that visually expresses key keywords by arranging related keywords so that they can be seen at a glance.

The mandalart has two functions. The first feature is the ability to organize or refine ideas around keywords. The second function is to help you achieve your goals. This app is focused on the second function and may not be suitable for those who are intended for the first function.

Mandalart itself may be unfamiliar because it is not a popular vocabulary and there are not many apps. To describe it using a popular app, it can be said to be more like a to do list app based on a mandalart.

Users set the core goal they want to achieve with the central keyword, define detailed goals for the core goal, and set specific action guidelines or mindsets for each detailed goal. And put it all in a frame called a mandalart so you can see it all at a glance. In this app, you can make a checklist by setting up routines among behavioral guidelines and mindsets. What sets this app apart from other mandalart apps is that you can create a checklist based on it, rather than just making a mandalart, and record it every day.

[ **Purchasing Policy** ]

This application does not use a subscription policy. It can be used with a single purchase, and services are not differentiated through in-app purchases after that. Updates apply equally to everyone.

[ Mandalart ]

This app starts by writing a mandalart.

A mandalart consists of 9 squares each horizontally and vertically. It consists of a total of 81 squares.

Each rectangle is filled with a goal and its related contents.

The core goal is in the center, and the detailed goals that make up the core goal are placed around the core goal.

And the periphery is the place for the detailed goal, and the detailed goal goes in the middle, and the Specific action guidelines and attitudes are included.

When using a mandalart for the purpose of achieving a goal, it is common to use one mandalart. So there is only one mandalart at a time.

[Checklist Settings ]

There may be actions or mindset for detailed goals that you want to check by organizing a checklist.

Select to configure the checklist. You can also specify a date if you want to check only on a specific date rather than include it in your daily checklist.

For example, it would not be appropriate to include the practice of "going to the gym three times a week" in the daily checklist.

[Record]

If you touch the date on the calendar inside the app, you can check what you did that day with the checklist you set and record what you want to record.

And the date with the record is marked on the calendar. The color concentration of the circle displayed in the calendar is the level of the checked items in the checklist The higher the specific gravity, the darker it is. 

So you can see the overall flow by looking at the change in the concentration of the circles shown in the calendar.

[History]

As mentioned earlier, there is only one mandalart at a time. In order to start a new journey by setting a new key goal, you need to delete the old mandalart. There was a user's opinion that it would be a pity to simply delete it, so we made it so that the existing mandalart can be saved. On the screen called History, you can save the existing mandalart and record your impressions so that you can look back on your past journey.

[Data Sync]
